utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you quote me an example from any television programme of the kind that you mention about inciting people to bloodshed? Because you say you believed the propaganda put out that civilians and children were being killed there. So my question to you was: Do you claim that all that was untrue, that in fact the Serbs were not under threat, and jeopardised them that it wasn't the civilians who were killed and people killed in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were crimes, that is true, caused by you through your policies and the aggression against Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I've already seen on Television Zagreb televised that they quote you. And that's just one single sentence that they do quote to the effect that the Serb forces launched the aggression against Croatia. Do you truly consider yourself to be competent in assessing whether Serb forces did perpetrate an aggression against Croatia or whether matters were quite different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say -- I'm saying what I saw. And you will know that best, because you were in Karadjordjevo with Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff she showed an exhibit and presented an exhibit and Mr. Kwon asked a question pertaining to it, because he received it just like myself. And he asked what the exhibit was about and what had happened to it. And the answer was that it wasn't too important, from the aspects and positions of this false indictment and false witnesses. Of course it is not important, if you look at it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The epithets you can leave out. We've heard them a great many times before. Now, what is it you're trying to refer to? Just a moment. Just a moment. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's Exhibit 387, tab 13. And I dropped it for time reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you want to ask a question about, you can, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which was returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We don't have our copies any more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title of this document are directives as to the use of the armed forces in the forthcoming period to prepare combat activities and operations. And the date is the 10th of December, 1991. "Directive on the use of the armed forces for the preparations and performance of combat operations in the forthcoming period." That is to say, after the events that we're discussing. It is signed by the federal secretary for National Defence, army General Veljko Kadijevic. And the page is 01061439. And I'm just going to quote a few portions in point 3, paragraph 3, for example. He says that the Yugoslav People's Army, together with the Territorial Defence in addition to initial weaknesses still managed to maintain its integrity and Yugoslav character. And then he goes on to say that "This had a significant influence on deblocking our forces in the Republic of Croatia." So my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where are we? First page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 3, "The Yugoslav People's Army and TO."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He talks about the Yugoslav People's Army and Territorial Defence. "Despite certain initial weaknesses, managed to retain its integrity and Yugoslav character, and this has contributed substantially to the relieving of our besieged forces in the Republic of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. C-047, do you know that the forces of the JNA, which had been there for 50 years, were actually blocked in the Republic of Croatia and had to withdraw, they had to leave. They were there protecting the population under jeopardy, they were there to protect mutual conflicts from breaking out? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the army was supposed to do. But the army didn't exist. It had already disintegrated in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned Borovo Selo, where through the intervention of the army the conflict was stopped and the army managed to save the group of Croatian policemen who were in Borovo Selo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And could you tell me what that army was composed of? The ethnic composition of the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm not here to answer your questions. You are here to answer mine but this is information that can be checked out easily, these facts and figures. Now, what I'm asking you is this: Did the army perpetrate an aggression against Croatia or was it blocked and attacked in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to enter into military matters as to what happened, when, and how. The army was on the territory of Croatia and we know why an armed conflict broke out. The Croatian civilians and in Bosnia the Muslims did not have any tanks or planes or cannons, as far as I know, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you know very little. But that is not the subject of your testimony anyway. That is self-evident, quite obvious. And then it goes on to say, "Considerable influence on deblocking our forces in Croatia and accepting the initiatives of the Presidency to involve the international peace forces in Yugoslavia." This is what it says. And then I would like to move on to page 3 of that same document, which was distributed here by the opposite side. So it wasn't me who brought the document in to the courtroom. It is point 6, or paragraph 6. It is an order by the federal secretary, dated December 1991. And paragraph 6 reads as follows: "In all zones of combat operations, place under the command of the most senior JNA officers all the units of the JNA and TO as well as volunteer units, which agree to be subordinate to that command and wear JNA and TO insignia. Consider all other armed formations paramilitaries, disarm them and remove them from the BD zone." Well, you've heard this. So how can you claim something you said yesterday, that is, that individual volunteers who went to join up, to join the JNA, and that they wore the insignia you showed us yesterday, the insignia of the Serbian Chetnik Movement and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you first of all, Mr. Milosevic, this was written down on paper but it is absolutely not true. The Serbian Volunteer Guard, let me tell you, with other insignia, the White Eagles, the Serbian Chetnik Movement, the Wolves of Bosnia and so on, they all had different insignia and patches. And the second point is it is not true that they disarmed and sent back the paramilitaries. We were under the command and did report to the commands in the area we were located as a Chetnik unit. However, we did not take down our insignias. We wore them. And you armed us, the Army of Yugoslavia, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Army of Yugoslavia armed you from you members of the Serbian Chetnik Movement? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to that in due course. But as far as I understood you yesterday, you explained to us that in Subotica you would obtain your weapons from the commander and his name, I think, was Colonel Jankovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Colonel Jankovic. It was Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine, Jovanovic, then. And then - and you can see this in the transcript - what you said was this: You said you were armed there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said who was under Colonel Jovanovic. I was in his presence when he asked to be sent weapons for Lika and he got them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the volunteers were armed by Colonel Jovanovic, garrison commander in Subotica. And then Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff asked you what happened when you arrived at the front, at the battlefield. Did you report to anybody? And you said yes, you did report to the military command there. Now -- and she asked you, "Why did you report?" And your answer was, "In order to be issued weapons, equipment, and accommodation." So Mr. C-047, in the same breath and in the space of several minutes of examination and cross-examination you first of all explained that you were armed by Colonel Jovanovic in Subotica and then in the same breath you say that once you had arrived you reported to the military command to receive weapons, et cetera, as a volunteer. Which of those two assertions is correct, Mr. C-047? Because you said both, and there is no printing error. What is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something quite different. I said who was with me. I said that we were in Colonel Jovanovic's apartment in Subotica, that he was provided with a list of the requests, and I saw uniforms and snipers, and they were taken from the 1st Barracks in Subotica. And the second point is that Dusko Stipanovic also took snipers from the barracks when he went to the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you know that there was a decision by the federal organs as to how volunteers were to be taken in, received? You say something about that, and you say that they had to have the psychological and physical properties they required, that they had to be normal people, no criminals among them, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are talking about. Not volunteers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know that there was a decision to take in volunteers according to set procedure and be deployed to the units and only in that way would they be considered to be full-fledged members of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they had to be healthy. They had to have done their military service. That was the basic requirement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have in your hands or before your eyes this decision by the Presidency of Yugoslavia as to the procedure? It was made public in the papers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that, but that referred to the volunteers in the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. So we've read what it says in the order of General Kadijevic, "All other armed formations should be considered paramilitary ones, should be disarmed, and excluded from combat operations." And then the next paragraph, it says: "With all measures prevent plunder, genocide, and retaliatory behaviour. Establish the necessary control by engaging the military police and other units designated for that purpose as well as criminal judicial organs." And then paragraph 7 says: "Contacts with the leaders of various parties should be made only in accordance with the regulations in force and with the prior consent of and in consultation with the higher command. In addition, undertake steps and avoid all compromising meetings with persons and representatives of anti-army propaganda." Is this the way in which the JNA related to the events that you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware at all that they acted in that way. Not a single volunteer unit, as far as I know, was turned back. They all wore their own insignia. As for looting and genocide, there was looting as there is in any war. The military police tried to prevent it. Nobody prevented Arkan. I don't know that any Chetnik from my unit or any area engaged in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. looting or genocide. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that they were not prevented. But towards the end of the examination-in-chief today, you said that you were in Skelani, that you left weapons there, that you were searched by the military police, that they searched everyone coming from Bosnia in order to seize their weapons. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I ordered the withdrawal of my unit. My unit was supposed to remain in the area of combat operations. I ordered the withdrawal. First of all, they wouldn't let us go. And afterwards, they let us go. There was a machine-gun pointed at us because we were leaving Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Fortunately not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it be quite the opposite? Didn't they chase you away from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went there on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you returned on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was difficult to go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you go back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then what have the authorities and the JNA to do with that? You went there as volunteers. You returned as volunteers. They seized your weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true that they seized our weapons. They didn't seize our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they searched you to find any weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't seize anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You returned with your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we returned the weapons at the school. People left their ammunition and grenades and what they had. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is what I'm talking about, the facts. So you went there as a volunteer unit. You stayed there. You left your weapons. And then you returned without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Could we go into private session to explain these things?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're wasting time. These are facts that have been covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness explain things that he wants to. He should be given a chance. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You provided some kind of diagram of the structure of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. It is on page 6, paragraph 5. And you say, talking about Vojvodina, that everything was centralised as the level of the province of Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was coming from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I saw this table of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tab 4. The witness can have it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it tab 4 or tab 7?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The SRS party chart is tab 4, and the Chetnik Movement chart is tab 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Taking advantage of some respite. I have to note the previous tab was tab 3, not 13 from the Exhibit 387.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you just one question with reference to tab 4, as you're explaining what was centralised. Looking from the bottom, you have one box in which it says -- from the top, "Vojislav Seselj, president." Then to the left and right, "The main board, responsible for Serbia, Republika Srpska, the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and others in Belgrade." And then "the Fatherland Administration." I don't know what the difference is between the main board and the fatherland board. But you as a member of the party probably know. And then the next box is: "The presidency of the Serbian Radical Party in Vojvodina." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The presidency of the Serbian Radical Party in Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say here Maja Gojkovic, president of the presidency of the Serbian Radical Party for Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in that Serbian Radical Party of yours, as you claim, there were no provincial levels? Because that is contrary to the political programme of your party, which advocated the abolition of provinces. There are no provincial levels in the Serbian Radical Party. There is a provincial level in the Socialist Party of Serbia but not in the -- do you know that as a party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that is not the point. Point of the Serbian Radical Party or the chain of command, if I can call it that, in the area in which I lived. That is what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You're talking about the chain of command. Then it would appear that Maja Gojkovic was your commander, a lady, an attorney from Novi Sad. She was commander of the Serbian Chetnik Movement in Vojvodina? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that -- mean that literally, but chain of management, chain of control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't like whichever way I put the question to you. You drew this chart, which doesn't correspond to the truth, because there's no provincial level. You say the chain of command and the head of the Serbian Chetnik Movement for you was Maja Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says for Vojvodina, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just we are looking at the structure of the SRS party. We are not looking at the Chetnik Movement. So I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your question is on the wrong premise, she says. Start with the Radical Party, then go on to the Chetnik Movement, if that's the point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have in mind the answers given by the witness. So allow me, therefore, to put some order into those answers. Because he says that is the chain of management of the Serbian Radical Party. Then he talks about the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may well be that he was misled by the questions and not taking one thing at a time. Just let's ask him about it. Start, if you would, with 4, tab 4, the structure of the SRS, which is what you were originally asked about, the Radical Party. How would you describe the relationship between your own -- or the municipal board and the -- say, the president of the Vojvodina party? Now, how would you describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Subotica, there was a municipal board and Subotica was the centre for several municipalities of the Serbian Radical Party, a political party, and for Northern Backa the president was Bozidar Vujic, and Ljubomir Rajic was president of the municipal board. The centre of this political party for Vojvodina - I'm talking about Vojvodina - was in Novi Sad, and Maja Gojkovic was president of the Serbian Party. As a coordinator for Vojvodina, for a while, Jovan Glamocanin held that position, and of course I also mentioned the president of the Serbian Radical Party, Vojislav Seselj in Belgrade. That was the chain I wanted to show, the political chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is not in dispute, the square that you have now -- the box that you have now explained, Maja Gojkovic, it says here, "Presidency of the Serbian Radical Party of Vojvodina. You wrote that, didn't you? That's what you think. You can think what you like. But the presidency of the Serbian Radical Party of Vojvodina does not exist, nor did it ever exist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't know then where I went to in Novi Sad. I went to Maja Gojkovic's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could have visited her in her office or in her home, but there's no presidency of the Serbian Radical Party of Vojvodina, according to their programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's pointless arguing about it. He says there was. If you have other information, you can put it in front of us. And if it's of any great importance, we can make a decision about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is important, Mr. May, as a very small point, and that is what is important is that this witness is giving us one untruth after another. That is all that is important, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is what you assert. It will be a matter for us to judge. Now, let us go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, pursuant to that logic, you can rule that today is Monday. There's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. C-047, you say - and you have it here on your chart - Maja Gojkovic was the deputy of Vojislav Seselj. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the officials in Belgrade, and she was for Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The position of deputy was introduced at the congress in May 1996, and the deputy Tomislav Nikolic and not Maja Gojkovic. She was never Seselj's deputy. You're talking about your own party.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume it would be logical for you to know things about your own party. But you're revealing an unbelievable lack of knowledge about a party of which you say you were a member.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling the truth. Now, whether she was the deputy and whether the presidency in Belgrade consisted of 10 or 15 members, Maja Gojkovic was one of them and she was in Novi Sad and she was in charge of Vojvodina and in charge of the municipal and inter-municipal boards of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no doubt that this lady was an official of the Serbian Radical Party, that she lives in Novi Sad, that she's an attorney at law, et cetera. But what I called in question was your whole chart and your allegations regarding the existence of institutions which do not exist. Have you read the programme of the party that was in force ever since 1991 to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Mr. Milosevic. What -- you said there was no centralisation. I am asking you now. You said there was no centralisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is something quite different. I am not entering into whether I agree or disagree with it. These are not my value judgements or yours, for that matter. They don't recognise provinces. They do not have organisations at provincial level. They don't have a provincial presidency. It is contrary to their programme to have this sort of structure as you drew it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am claiming that they do have them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are even claiming that Vujic and Radic were kums or -- I wanted that to be checked out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that too is incorrect. I know both very well. Mr. Radic is an employee of the state security. Let me tell you that too. Ljubomir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the information I have received, it is true that there is a Radic who's a kum to Vujic but he's not Ljubomir Radic from the DB but Gojko Radic, which has nothing in common with this person. And a best man at a wedding can with checked out in the marriage certificate. It is registered in the registrar of married couples. It's not difficult to check out. To say things just like that, as you believe will be convincing, there's no point in that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: Mr. Radic and his kum were employees of the state security in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on as far as that is concerned. I tried to put a question to you about it, but obviously your information is different. You talk about cards of volunteers from the Serbian Chetnik Movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never used the word "iskaznica".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what it says on page 8, paragraphs 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people translating this probably used their own language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't translated from English into Serbian, but I assume from Serbian into English.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that important? As if you didn't know what an "iskaznica" is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you gave such a statement, I wanted to check out what is stated in your statement. And as everything has proven to be incorrect, among other things this too that there were no "iskaznica" or membership cards?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's not a proper question and another comment by you. It's inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. It's an inappropriate question, then, Mr. May to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that no way of IDs by way of "iskaznica" existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Iskaznica" is what existed in Croatia. Whereas here there were membership cards for acceding to the membership, "pristupnica".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of the information I have - and please be so kind as to confirm this or deny it - so there are no such papers. Volunteers would give their personal IDs, their military IDs, and a written statement to the effect that they were not ill physically or mentally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about these illnesses, but the personal IDs, that's true. And also the military IDs, the military booklets, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they did not say whether they were physically or mentally ill or whether they were drug addicts or something like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Milosevic, I'm not a doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what you've been saying, should there be some files of volunteers in Subotica in the archives of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There should be files. I don't have anything. Had I had this and had this been found on me, the members of your state security service would have killed me a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was killed on the basis of what you know? Who was killed by the members of the state security service of Serbia? It's a different thing what you said about arrests. I mean, yes, arrests they would have carried out. But what about killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't really want to discuss that. It is known in Serbia what happened and who was engaged in killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who knows? I imagine this is something that is known.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope that this is known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, since you are linking up the MUP, are you trying to say that in the Ministry of the Interior there was some kind of a command structure of the Serb Chetnik Movement? You have this on page 7 in paragraph 3. You talk about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what kind of an invention is this fabrication? Look what it says. This is nothing that reveals who you are. You say, "Chain of command of the Serb Radical Party in the SUP was the following." And at the top there is DB Belgrade, which is to say the state security commands the Serb Radical Party; right? Does the state security command the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was cooperation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a minute. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are sticking to this word "command." I'm talking about the linkage between the leaders. The SUP, Mr. Milosevic, the top people of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please, take a look at this. I mean, I really have to read this for the public. You say: "Chain of command of the Serb Radical Party in the SUP is the following," and then it says, "DB Belgrade on the top." And then "the intercommunal SUP of the northern Backa district. And below it says Milan Jerinkic, secretary of the SUP, Northern Backa district, member of the Serb Radical Party. And then Radovan Knezevic, head of the Northern Backa SUP district, sympathiser of the Serb Radical Party. And then Mirko Zinanic, chief of SUP in fact town of Subotica, member of the Serb Radical Party. And then Nikola Ivosevic, chief operations in the Northern Backa direct, member of the Serb Radical Party. And finally -- and finally, now, let me not go into that, lest we reveal any identities. What is this, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-047 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You find this ridiculous, Mr. Milosevic, but these people are members of the Serb Radical Party or sympathisers of the Serb Radical Party. They were top people in the Northern Backa District and they were members of the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. C-047, I told you that these people whose names I mentioned were not members of the Serb Radical Party. But even if things were the way you put them, even if they were sympathisers, I mean someone can be a sympathiser of the Red Star Soccer Club and somebody else of the Partisan Soccer Club?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You will conduct this in an orderly way. Are you suggesting that the witness is wrong when he says that these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. people were members of the Serb Radical Party? Is this the point of all of this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two points, Mr. May: One is that this is a lie; the second point is that even if it were not, what kind of chain of command is this of the Serb Radical Party and the SUP? Because you say that the DB, the state security, is on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness -- the witness can now deal with this. You've already told us that -- what the witness -- what the accused says is wrong and in fact these people were members of the Serb Radical Party. So there's no need to repeat that. But the other point is this: You are being asked about what sort of a chain of command was it with the Serb Radical Party and the SUP. Was the DB on the top? Now, you can answer it, and if you want you can answer it in this -- if you prefer, you can answer in a private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be better to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean that we are going to adjourn for the day, that we are not going to put any more questions today? Or should I just complete this topic that I've been dealing with now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We've got to finish, because there's another hearing coming into this courtroom. Witness C-047, that concludes your evidence for the moment. We will try and reach you tomorrow, to try and finish it. The accused has an hour and a quarter left for cross-examination. We will try and, as I say, fit that in tomorrow if we can. But meanwhile, we will go on with B-024, and then B-1098. We'll adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow morning.
